_description: Deterministic ranking contract - the exact signals and weights search/headless-search-prototype.mjs implements, tested against search/search-query-fixtures.json. No ML, no embeddings, no external service - a scored, explainable pipeline a future UI can call as-is or reimplement identically in a different language.
pipeline: 1. Normalize the query (see search-typo-tolerance-contract in SEARCH-DESIGN-HANDOFF.md - lowercase, strip diacritics/punctuation, collapse whitespace).

2. Resolve aliases: if the normalized query exactly matches an entry in search-aliases.json's `alias` or `aliasSlugLowercased`, retarget the query to that alias's `targetId` and continue scoring normally against the target document (not a special-cased short-circuit - the target still competes on its own merits, it just starts from the alias match signal below).
3. Expand synonyms: for each token in the query, look up search-synonyms.json; if a match is found, add the equivalents as additional query tokens for matching purposes only (never for display).
4. Classify query intent (see queryIntentSignals below) - zero or more of the 8 intents from search-taxonomy.json.
5. Score every document (see signals below), sum, apply content-type balancing, sort descending, return.

signals.description: normalized query string equals normalized document title exactly
query resolved via search-aliases.json to this document
normalized query exactly equals a keyword in the document's own `keywords[]` (covers acronyms like 'CAC', 'ROAS', journey ids like 'ACC-71', ab-test ids like 'AB-001')
normalized document title starts with the normalized query
each query token (post-synonym-expansion) found as a whole word in the title
each query token found in keywords[]
each query token found in category[] or normalizedCategory[] (case-insensitive substring)
each query token found in surface[] or funnelStage[]
each query token found in metric[] (post-synonym-expansion, so 'return on ad spend' matches a metric field of 'ROAS')
the document's own default intent set (search-taxonomy.json's defaultIntentByType) intersects the query's classified intent(s)
each query token found anywhere in searchText - the lowest-weight signal, catches genuine full-text relevance without letting a long searchText dominate a short, precise title/keyword match
a small, fixed per-type nudge - NOT a substitute for relevance, just breaks ties toward the type most likely to be the primary target of a well-matched query

boostByType.reasoning: calculator gets a small edge because it's the most 'answer a specific question fast' type on the site (matches the calculate/use-tool intents), and lab-product gets a small edge because it's the entry point to an entire corpus, useful when a query is genuinely ambiguous between browsing and a specific item. blog-article is nudged slightly down only because there are just 5 of them and a title/keyword match against 520 other documents is already a strong enough signal without a boost. None of these differences are large enough to override a real relevance gap - see the content-type balancing note below for what actually prevents one type from monopolizing results.

queryIntentSignals._description: Query-time intent classification - lightweight keyword heuristics, not a hardcoded single-result mapping (per the task's own instruction that these must function as ranking signals, not forced routing).
queryIntentSignals.note: find-example has no dedicated trigger list - it's produced as a secondary intent whenever 'find-test' or 'find-journey' fires, since both corpora are themselves collections of examples. A query can classify into multiple intents at once (e.g. 'cart abandonment test' -> find-test + find-example); all classified intents contribute to intent-match scoring, none suppress the others.

contentTypeBalancing._description: Prevents one type from monopolizing a broad query's results (task's own example: a 'conversion' search shouldn't return 10/10 journeys) WITHOUT overriding genuine relevance gaps.
contentTypeBalancing.rule: After scoring and sorting, if the top 10 results contain more than 6 documents of the same type AND at least one lower-ranked document of a different type scores within 30% of the 10th-place score, promote that document above the 30%-threshold cutoff into the top 10 (a soft diversity floor, not a hard reshuffle). If no other-type document is within 30%, leave the ranking as-is - relevance wins over diversity when the gap is real.
contentTypeBalancing.verifiedAgainstFixtures: search-query-fixtures.json includes cases designed to exercise this rule (broad terms like 'conversion', 'checkout') - see search/headless-search-prototype.mjs's own test output for whether the rule actually fired on those queries in this corpus.

tieBreaking: equal total score -> higher boostByType wins -> alphabetical by title (deterministic, never random) as the final fallback.
